entry.summary: Most web scraping tutorials focus on the micro view: how to extract the price of a single laptop or the specs of a specific blender. While price monitoring is useful, it doesn't tell you why a competitor is winning. To understand a competitor's true market position, you need to zoom out and look at the macro view, the Assortment Mix. The assortment mix represents the total variety and depth of products a retailer stocks. By programmatically scraping entire product categories, you can reverse-engineer a competitor's strategy. This data reveals which brands they prioritize, where they have inventory gaps, and which price tiers they are betting on. entry.title: Rejected but Not Defeated: Continuing My Journey Toward AWS Community Builders
entry.summary:
I recently received the news that I was not selected for the Amazon Web Services (AWS) Community Builders Program this year. Yes, it is disappointing. But I see this as redirection, not rejection. As a career shifter, breaking into tech and cloud has never been the easy path. It has required discipline, late nights of studying, continuous upskilling, and the courage to start over. This moment does not define my journey. It fuels it. I remain fully committed to growing within the AWS ecosystem. My focus is to deepen my expertise as a Data Engineer in AWS, especially in data services, databases, and analytics tools. More importantly, I will continue sharing what I learn with others who are interested in data and analytics, even when resources are limited. Access to knowledge should not depend on background or budget.
I still aspire to be part of the AWS Community Builders team. I will reapply next year with stronger contributions, greater community involvement, and more impact to show. Growth is not built on acceptance alone. It is built on resilience, consistency, and the decision to keep going. And I am just getting started.
